raw: MARCH 15.

translation.en: March 15
translation.kr: 3월 15일

raw: I have just had a sad adventure, which will drive me away from here. I lose all patience!—Death!—It is not to be remedied; and you alone are to blame, for you urged and impelled me to fill a post for which I was by no means suited. I have now reason to be satisfied, and so have you! But, that you may not again attribute this fatality to my impetuous temper, I send you, my dear sir, a plain and simple narration of the affair, as a mere chronicler of facts would describe it.

translation.en: I have just had a sad adventure, which will drive me away from here.
translation.kr: 방금 서글픈 일을 하나 겪었네. 그 일로 나는 이곳을 떠나게 될 걸세.

translation.en: I lose all patience! Death! There is no remedy for it; and you alone are to blame, for you urged and pushed me into a post I was by no means suited to.
translation.kr: 참을 수가 없네! 죽을 노릇이야! 이제 돌이킬 방도가 없고, 그것은 오로지 자네 탓일세. 나와는 도무지 맞지 않는 자리에 나를 떠밀어 넣은 것이 자네이니.

translation.en: I have reason to be satisfied now, and so have you!
translation.kr: 이제 나도 만족스럽고, 자네도 만족스럽겠지!

translation.en: But so that you may not again put this disaster down to my impetuous temper, I send you, my dear sir, a plain and simple account of the affair, such as a mere chronicler of facts would give.
translation.kr: 그러나 이 낭패를 또 내 조급한 성미 탓으로 돌리지 않도록, 친애하는 벗이여, 사실을 적는 기록자가 하듯 담담하고 간단하게 그 일을 적어 보내겠네.

raw: The Count of O— likes and distinguishes me. It is well known, and I have mentioned this to you a hundred times. Yesterday I dined with him. It is the day on which the nobility are accustomed to assemble at his house in the evening. I never once thought of the assembly, nor that we subalterns did not belong to such society. Well, I dined with the count; and, after dinner, we adjourned to the large hall. We walked up and down together: and I conversed with him, and with Colonel B—, who joined us; and in this manner the hour for the assembly approached. God knows, I was thinking of nothing, when who should enter but the honourable Lady accompanied by her noble husband and their silly, scheming daughter, with her small waist and flat neck; and, with disdainful looks and a haughty air they passed me by. As I heartily detest the whole race, I determined upon going away; and only waited till the count had disengaged himself from their impertinent prattle, to take leave, when the agreeable Miss B— came in. As I never meet her without experiencing a heartfelt pleasure, I stayed and talked to her, leaning over the back of her chair, and did not perceive, till after some time, that she seemed a little confused, and ceased to answer me with her usual ease of manner. I was struck with it. "Heavens!" I said to myself, "can she, too, be like the rest?" I felt annoyed, and was about to withdraw; but I remained, notwithstanding, forming excuses for her conduct, fancying she did not mean it, and still hoping to receive some friendly recognition. The rest of the company now arrived. There was the Baron F—, in an entire suit that dated from the coronation of Francis I.; the Chancellor N—, with his deaf wife; the shabbily-dressed I—, whose old-fashioned coat bore evidence of modern repairs: this crowned the whole. I conversed with some of my acquaintances, but they answered me laconically. I was engaged in observing Miss B—, and did not notice that the women were whispering at the end of the room, that the murmur extended by degrees to the men, that Madame S— addressed the count with much warmth (this was all related to me subsequently by Miss B—); till at length the count came up to me, and took me to the window. "You know our ridiculous customs," he said. "I perceive the company is rather displeased at your being here. I would not on any account—" "I beg your excellency's pardon!" I exclaimed. "I ought to have thought of this before, but I know you will forgive this little inattention. I was going," I added, "some time ago, but my evil genius detained me." And I smiled and bowed, to take my leave. He shook me by the hand, in a manner which expressed everything. I hastened at once from the illustrious assembly, sprang into a carriage, and drove to M—. I contemplated the setting sun from the top of the hill, and read that beautiful passage in Homer, where Ulysses is entertained by the hospitable herdsmen. This was indeed delightful.

translation.en: The Count of O— likes me and singles me out.
translation.kr: O 백작은 나를 좋아하고 각별히 대해 주네.

translation.en: That is well known, and I have told you so a hundred times.
translation.kr: 잘 알려진 일이고, 자네에게도 백 번은 말했지.

translation.en: Yesterday I dined with him.
translation.kr: 어제 그와 함께 식사를 했네.

translation.en: It is the day on which the nobility are accustomed to gather at his house in the evening.
translation.kr: 저녁이면 귀족들이 그 집에 모이는 날이었지.

translation.en: I never once thought of the assembly, nor that we subalterns do not belong in such company.
translation.kr: 나는 그 모임 생각은 조금도 하지 못했고, 우리 같은 하급 관리는 그런 자리에 낄 사람이 아니라는 것도 떠올리지 못했네.

translation.en: Well, I dined with the count; and after dinner we went through to the large hall.
translation.kr: 여하튼 백작과 식사를 하고, 식사 뒤에 우리는 큰 홀로 건너갔네.

translation.en: We walked up and down together, and I talked with him, and with Colonel B—, who joined us; and so the hour of the assembly came on.
translation.kr: 함께 거닐며 이야기를 나누었고, 도중에 합류한 B 대령과도 이야기했네. 그러는 사이 모임 시간이 다가왔지.

translation.en: God knows I was thinking of nothing, when in came the honourable Lady with her noble husband and their silly, scheming daughter, with her small waist and flat neck; and with disdainful looks and a haughty air they passed me by.
translation.kr: 정말이지 아무 생각 없이 있었는데, 그때 그 귀하신 부인이 고귀한 남편과, 허리가 가늘고 목이 밋밋한 그 어리석고 속 빠른 딸을 데리고 들어섰네. 그리고 업신여기는 눈길과 거만한 태도로 내 앞을 지나쳐 갔네.

translation.en: As I heartily detest the whole breed, I decided to go; and I was only waiting for the count to free himself from their impertinent prattle so that I could take my leave, when the agreeable Miss B— came in.
translation.kr: 나는 그 족속 전체를 진심으로 혐오하는 터라 그만 가려고 마음먹었네. 그래서 백작이 그들의 무례한 수다에서 벗어나기를 기다려 작별을 고하려던 참에, 상냥한 B 양이 들어왔네.

translation.en: As I never meet her without a heartfelt pleasure, I stayed and talked to her, leaning over the back of her chair, and it was some time before I noticed that she seemed a little confused, and had stopped answering me with her usual ease.
translation.kr: 그이를 만날 때면 늘 진심으로 반가운 터라, 나는 남아서 의자 등받이에 몸을 기댄 채 이야기를 나누었네. 그러다 한참 뒤에야 그이가 좀 당황한 듯하고, 여느 때처럼 편하게 대답하지 않는다는 것을 알아챘네.

translation.en: It struck me.
translation.kr: 나는 흠칫했네.

translation.en: "Heavens!" I said to myself. "Can she be like the rest of them too?"
translation.kr: "이럴 수가!" 나는 속으로 생각했네. "이 사람도 다른 자들과 같단 말인가?"

translation.en: I felt annoyed and was on the point of leaving; but I stayed all the same, making excuses for her, fancying she did not mean it, and still hoping for some friendly sign.
translation.kr: 짜증이 나서 나가려다가, 그래도 남았네. 그이를 두둔해 보고, 본심은 아니려니 여기고, 그래도 다정한 기색 하나쯤은 보이려니 기대하면서.

translation.en: The rest of the company now arrived.
translation.kr: 그러는 사이 나머지 사람들이 들어왔네.

translation.en: There was Baron F—, in a whole suit dating from the coronation of Francis I; the Chancellor N—, with his deaf wife; and the shabbily dressed I—, whose old-fashioned coat showed evidence of modern repairs, which crowned the whole.
translation.kr: 프란츠 1세 대관식 때 지었을 법한 옷을 통째로 걸친 F 남작, 귀먹은 아내를 데려온 N 재상, 그리고 낡은 옷에 요즘 식으로 기운 자국이 뚜렷한 초라한 차림의 I— 씨가 있었는데, 그것으로 화룡점정이었지.

translation.en: I talked with some of my acquaintances, but they answered me in monosyllables.
translation.kr: 아는 사람 몇과 이야기를 나누었네만, 다들 단답으로만 응했네.

translation.en: I was busy watching Miss B—, and did not notice that the women were whispering at the end of the room, that the murmur was spreading by degrees to the men, and that Madame S— was addressing the count very warmly.
translation.kr: 나는 B 양을 살피느라, 방 끝에서 여자들이 수군거리는 것도, 그 웅성거림이 차츰 남자들에게 번지는 것도, S 부인이 백작에게 몹시 열을 올려 말하는 것도 알아채지 못했네.

translation.en: All this was related to me afterwards by Miss B—.
translation.kr: 이 모든 것은 나중에 B 양이 들려준 이야기일세.

translation.en: At length the count came up to me and took me over to the window.
translation.kr: 마침내 백작이 내게 다가와 창가로 데려갔네.

translation.en: "You know our ridiculous customs," he said.
translation.kr: "우리의 우스운 관례를 아시지요." 그가 말했네.

translation.en: "I see that the company is rather displeased at your being here. I would not on any account —"
translation.kr: "당신이 여기 있는 것을 사람들이 좀 언짢아하는 듯합니다. 저로서야 결코 —"

translation.en: "I beg your excellency's pardon!" I exclaimed.
translation.kr: "각하, 용서를 구합니다!" 내가 외쳤네.

translation.en: "I ought to have thought of it before, but I know you will forgive this little inattention."
translation.kr: "진작 헤아렸어야 했습니다. 이 작은 부주의를 용서해 주시리라 믿습니다."

translation.en: "I was going some time ago," I added, "but my evil genius kept me here."
translation.kr: "아까부터 가려던 참이었습니다." 내가 덧붙였네. "그런데 제 못된 운이 저를 붙들어 두었군요."

translation.en: And I smiled and bowed, and took my leave.
translation.kr: 그러고는 웃으며 고개를 숙이고 자리를 떴네.

translation.en: He shook me by the hand in a way that said everything.
translation.kr: 그는 모든 것을 말해 주는 손길로 내 손을 잡아 흔들었네.

translation.en: I hurried straight out of the illustrious assembly, sprang into a carriage, and drove to M—.
translation.kr: 나는 그 고귀한 모임에서 곧장 빠져나와 마차에 뛰어올라 M—으로 달렸네.

translation.en: I watched the sun set from the top of the hill, and read that beautiful passage in Homer where Ulysses is entertained by the hospitable herdsmen.
translation.kr: 언덕 꼭대기에서 해가 지는 것을 보며, 오디세우스가 인정 많은 목자들의 대접을 받는 호메로스의 그 아름다운 대목을 읽었네.

translation.en: That was delightful indeed.
translation.kr: 그것은 참으로 좋았네.

raw: I returned home to supper in the evening. But few persons were assembled in the room. They had turned up a corner of the table-cloth, and were playing at dice. The good-natured A— came in. He laid down his hat when he saw me, approached me, and said in a low tone, "You have met with a disagreeable adventure." "I!" I exclaimed. "The count obliged you to withdraw from the assembly!" "Deuce take the assembly!" said I. "I was very glad to be gone." "I am delighted," he added, "that you take it so lightly. I am only sorry that it is already so much spoken of." The circumstance then began to pain me. I fancied that every one who sat down, and even looked at me, was thinking of this incident; and my heart became embittered.

translation.en: I came home to supper in the evening.
translation.kr: 저녁에 집에 돌아와 밥상을 받았네.

translation.en: There were only a few people in the room.
translation.kr: 방에는 몇 사람밖에 없었네.

translation.en: They had turned back a corner of the tablecloth and were playing dice.
translation.kr: 식탁보 한쪽을 걷어 올리고 주사위 놀이를 하고 있더군.

translation.en: The good-natured A— came in.
translation.kr: 마음씨 좋은 A— 씨가 들어왔네.

translation.en: He laid down his hat when he saw me, came over, and said in a low voice, "You have met with a disagreeable adventure."
translation.kr: 나를 보고는 모자를 내려놓고 다가와 나직이 말했네. "언짢은 일을 겪으셨더군요."

translation.en: "I!" I exclaimed.
translation.kr: "내가요!" 나는 외쳤네.

translation.en: "The count obliged you to leave the assembly!"
translation.kr: "백작이 모임에서 나가라고 하셨다면서요."

translation.en: "Deuce take the assembly!" said I.
translation.kr: "그런 모임 따위!" 하고 내가 말했네.

translation.en: "I was very glad to be out of it."
translation.kr: "나오게 되어 오히려 다행이었습니다."

translation.en: "I am delighted," he added, "that you take it so lightly."
translation.kr: "그렇게 가볍게 여기시니" 하고 그가 덧붙였네. "저도 마음이 놓입니다."

translation.en: "I am only sorry that it is already so much talked about."
translation.kr: "다만 벌써 그 이야기가 이렇게 돌고 있다는 것이 안타깝습니다."

translation.en: It was then that the thing began to hurt.
translation.kr: 그제야 그 일이 아프기 시작했네.

translation.en: I fancied that everyone who sat down, or even looked at me, was thinking of this incident; and my heart grew bitter.
translation.kr: 자리에 앉는 사람마다, 나를 쳐다보는 사람마다 그 일을 떠올리고 있는 것만 같았고, 내 마음은 쓰디써졌네.

raw: And now I could plunge a dagger into my bosom, when I hear myself everywhere pitied, and observe the triumph of my enemies, who say that this is always the case with vain persons, whose heads are turned with conceit, who affect to despise forms and such petty, idle nonsense.

translation.en: And now I could plunge a dagger into my breast, when I hear myself pitied on every side, and see the triumph of my enemies.
translation.kr: 그리고 사방에서 나를 딱하게 여기는 소리를 듣고 내 적들이 우쭐대는 꼴을 보고 있자니, 지금이라도 가슴에 단검을 꽂고 싶네.

translation.en: This is always the way with vain people, they say — people whose heads are turned with conceit, who make a show of despising forms and such petty, idle nonsense.
translation.kr: 허영에 찬 자들은 늘 저렇다고들 하네 — 자만으로 머리가 돌아, 격식이니 그 따위 하찮고 부질없는 것들을 우습게 아는 척하는 자들 말일세.

raw: Say what you will of fortitude, but show me the man who can patiently endure the laughter of fools, when they have obtained an advantage over him. 'Tis only when their nonsense is without foundation that one can suffer it without complaint.

translation.en: Say what you like about fortitude, but show me the man who can patiently endure the laughter of fools when they have got the advantage of him.
translation.kr: 꿋꿋함을 두고 무어라 하든, 바보들이 저를 이겼다고 웃어 댈 때 그것을 참아 낼 수 있는 사람을 내게 보여 주게.

translation.en: It is only when their nonsense has no foundation that one can bear it without complaint.
translation.kr: 그 시답잖은 소리에 근거가 없을 때라야 군말 없이 견딜 수 있는 법일세.

raw: March 16.

translation.en: March 16.

raw: Everything conspires against me. I met Miss B— walking to-day. I could not help joining her; and, when we were at a little distance from her companions, I expressed my sense of her altered manner toward me. "O Werther!" she said, in a tone of emotion, "you, who know my heart, how could you so ill interpret my distress? What did I not suffer for you, from the moment you entered the room! I foresaw it all, a hundred times was I on the point of mentioning it to you. I knew that the S——s and T——s, with their husbands, would quit the room, rather than remain in your company. I knew that the count would not break with them: and now so much is said about it." "How!" I exclaimed, and endeavoured to conceal my emotion; for all that Adelin had mentioned to me yesterday recurred to me painfully at that moment. "Oh, how much it has already cost me!" said this amiable girl, while her eyes filled with tears. I could scarcely contain myself, and was ready to throw myself at her feet. "Explain yourself!" I cried. Tears flowed down her cheeks. I became quite frantic. She wiped them away, without attempting to conceal them. "You know my aunt," she continued; "she was present: and in what light does she consider the affair! Last night, and this morning, Werther, I was compelled to listen to a lecture upon my acquaintance with you. I have been obliged to hear you condemned and depreciated; and I could not—I dared not—say much in your defence."

translation.en: Everything conspires against me.
translation.kr: 모든 것이 나를 거스르네.

translation.en: I met Miss B— out walking today.
translation.kr: 오늘 산책하다 B 양을 만났네.

translation.en: I could not help joining her; and when we were a little way from her companions, I told her I had felt the change in her manner toward me.
translation.kr: 함께 걷지 않을 수 없었고, 동행들에게서 조금 떨어졌을 때 나는 나를 대하는 태도가 달라진 것을 느꼈다고 말했네.

translation.en: "O Werther!" she said, in a tone of emotion, "you, who know my heart, how could you so misread my distress?"
translation.kr: "아, 베르테르 씨!" 그이가 감정이 북받친 목소리로 말했네. "제 마음을 아시는 분이 어떻게 제 괴로움을 그렇게 잘못 읽으셨어요?"

translation.en: "What did I not suffer for you, from the moment you came into that room!"
translation.kr: "그 방에 들어오시던 순간부터 제가 얼마나 마음을 졸였는지 아세요!"

translation.en: "I foresaw it all; a hundred times I was on the point of telling you."
translation.kr: "저는 다 내다보고 있었어요. 백 번도 더 말씀드리려다 말았지요."

translation.en: "I knew that the S——s and T——s, with their husbands, would leave the room rather than stay in your company."
translation.kr: "S 댁 사람들과 T 댁 사람들이 남편들까지 데리고, 당신과 한자리에 있느니 방을 나가 버리리라는 것을 알고 있었어요."

translation.en: "I knew the count would not break with them — and now there is so much talk about it."
translation.kr: "백작이 그들과 등지지 않으리라는 것도 알았고요 — 그런데 이제 말이 이렇게 많아졌네요."

translation.en: "How!" I exclaimed, and tried to hide my emotion; for everything Adelin had told me the day before came back painfully at that moment.
translation.kr: "이런!" 나는 외치며 감정을 감추려 했네. 어제 아델린이 들려준 이야기가 모두 그 순간 아프게 되살아났던 것일세.

translation.en: "Oh, how much it has already cost me!" said this amiable girl, while her eyes filled with tears.
translation.kr: "아, 저는 벌써 얼마나 치렀는지 몰라요!" 그 상냥한 아가씨가 눈에 눈물을 글썽이며 말했네.

translation.en: I could scarcely contain myself, and was ready to throw myself at her feet.
translation.kr: 나는 도무지 나를 다잡을 수 없어 그 발치에 몸을 던질 뻔했네.

translation.en: "Explain yourself!" I cried.
translation.kr: "무슨 말씀인지 말해 주세요!" 나는 소리쳤네.

translation.en: Tears ran down her cheeks.
translation.kr: 눈물이 그 뺨을 타고 흘렀네.

translation.en: I became quite frantic.
translation.kr: 나는 거의 제정신이 아니었네.

translation.en: She wiped them away without trying to hide them.
translation.kr: 그이는 눈물을 감추려 하지도 않고 닦아 냈네.

translation.en: "You know my aunt," she went on. "She was there — and in what light do you suppose she sees the affair!"
translation.kr: "제 숙모를 아시지요." 그이가 말을 이었네. "그 자리에 계셨어요 — 그러니 그 일을 어떻게 보셨겠어요!"

translation.en: "Last night, and again this morning, Werther, I had to sit through a lecture on my acquaintance with you."
translation.kr: "어젯밤에도 오늘 아침에도, 베르테르 씨, 저는 당신과 알고 지내는 것에 대한 훈계를 꼼짝없이 들어야 했어요."

translation.en: "I have had to hear you condemned and belittled, and I could not — I dared not — say much in your defence."
translation.kr: "당신이 헐뜯기고 깎아내려지는 것을 들어야 했는데, 저는 당신을 두둔하는 말을 많이 할 수도 — 감히 할 수도 없었어요."

raw: Every word she uttered was a dagger to my heart. She did not feel what a mercy it would have been to conceal everything from me. She told me, in addition, all the impertinence that would be further circulated, and how the malicious would triumph; how they would rejoice over the punishment of my pride, over my humiliation for that want of esteem for others with which I had often been reproached. To hear all this, Wilhelm, uttered by her in a voice of the most sincere sympathy, awakened all my passions; and I am still in a state of extreme excitement. I wish I could find a man to jeer me about this event. I would sacrifice him to my resentment. The sight of his blood might possibly be a relief to my fury. A hundred times have I seized a dagger, to give ease to this oppressed heart. Naturalists tell of a noble race of horses that instinctively open a vein with their teeth, when heated and exhausted by a long course, in order to breathe more freely. I am often tempted to open a vein, to procure for myself everlasting liberty.

translation.en: Every word she said was a dagger in my heart.
translation.kr: 그이가 하는 말 한마디 한마디가 내 가슴에 꽂히는 단검이었네.

translation.en: She did not feel what a mercy it would have been to keep all of it from me.
translation.kr: 그 모든 것을 내게 감추어 주었더라면 얼마나 자비로운 일이었을지 그이는 알지 못했네.

translation.en: She told me besides all the impertinence that would go on circulating, and how the malicious would gloat.
translation.kr: 게다가 앞으로도 돌아다닐 무례한 말들과, 악의를 품은 자들이 얼마나 고소해할지까지 다 들려주었네.

translation.en: How they would rejoice at the punishment of my pride, at my humiliation for that want of regard for others I have so often been reproached with.
translation.kr: 내 자존심이 꺾인 것을, 남을 배려할 줄 모른다고 그토록 자주 책잡히던 내가 망신당한 것을 그들이 얼마나 기뻐할지를 말일세.

translation.en: To hear all this, Wilhelm, spoken by her in a voice of the most sincere sympathy, roused every passion in me; and I am still in a state of extreme agitation.
translation.kr: 빌헬름, 더없이 진심 어린 연민의 목소리로 그이가 이 모든 것을 말하는 것을 듣고 있자니 내 안의 온갖 격정이 일어섰네. 나는 아직도 몹시 흥분해 있네.

translation.en: I wish I could find a man to jeer at me about this business.
translation.kr: 이 일로 나를 비웃어 줄 사람 하나를 만났으면 싶네.

translation.en: I would sacrifice him to my resentment.
translation.kr: 그자를 내 원한의 제물로 바치겠네.

translation.en: The sight of his blood might possibly relieve my fury.
translation.kr: 그 피를 보면 어쩌면 이 광기가 가라앉을지도 모르지.

translation.en: A hundred times I have taken up a dagger to give this oppressed heart some ease.
translation.kr: 짓눌린 이 가슴을 좀 풀어 주려고 나는 백 번이나 단검을 집어 들었네.

translation.en: Naturalists tell of a noble breed of horses that instinctively open a vein with their teeth when they are heated and exhausted by a long run, in order to breathe more freely.
translation.kr: 박물학자들 말로는, 오래 달려 열이 오르고 기진한 고귀한 종자의 말들은 숨을 더 잘 쉬려고 본능적으로 제 이로 핏줄을 연다더군.

translation.en: I am often tempted to open a vein, and secure myself everlasting liberty.
translation.kr: 나도 자주 핏줄을 열어 영원한 자유를 얻고 싶은 유혹을 느끼네.

raw: MARCH 24.

translation.en: March 24
translation.kr: 3월 24일

raw: I have tendered my resignation to the court. I hope it will be accepted, and you will forgive me for not having previously consulted you. It is necessary I should leave this place. I know all you will urge me to stay, and therefore I beg you will soften this news to my mother. I am unable to do anything for myself: how, then, should I be competent to assist others? It will afflict her that I should have interrupted that career which would have made me first a privy councillor, and then minister, and that I should look behind me, in place of advancing. Argue as you will, combine all the reasons which should have induced me to remain, I am going: that is sufficient. But, that you may not be ignorant of my destination, I may mention that the Prince of —— is here. He is much pleased with my company; and, having heard of my intention to resign, he has invited me to his country house, to pass the spring months with him. I shall be left completely my own master; and, as we agree on all subjects but one, I shall try my fortune, and accompany him.

translation.en: I have tendered my resignation to the court.
translation.kr: 나는 궁정에 사직서를 냈네.

translation.en: I hope it will be accepted, and you will forgive me for not having consulted you first.
translation.kr: 받아들여지기를 바라네. 그리고 자네와 먼저 의논하지 않은 것은 용서해 주게.

translation.en: It is necessary that I leave this place.
translation.kr: 나는 이곳을 떠나야만 하네.

translation.en: I know everything you will say to make me stay, and so I beg you will soften the news to my mother.
translation.kr: 나를 붙들려고 자네가 할 말은 다 알고 있으니, 부디 어머니께는 이 소식을 부드럽게 전해 주게.

translation.en: I am unable to do anything for myself; how then should I be fit to help others?
translation.kr: 나 하나도 어쩌지 못하는 내가, 어떻게 남을 도울 만하겠는가?

translation.en: It will grieve her that I should have broken off the career that would have made me first a privy councillor and then a minister, and that I should be looking backwards instead of advancing.
translation.kr: 먼저 추밀 고문관이 되고 다음에 장관이 되었을 그 길을 내가 끊어 버린 것, 앞으로 나아가는 대신 뒤를 돌아보는 것이 어머니께는 서운하시겠지.

translation.en: Argue as you like, gather up every reason that should have kept me here — I am going, and that is enough.
translation.kr: 무어라 따지든, 나를 여기 붙들어 둘 온갖 이유를 다 끌어모으든 — 나는 가네. 그것으로 되었네.

translation.en: But so that you may know where I am bound, I may mention that the Prince of —— is here.
translation.kr: 다만 내가 어디로 가는지는 알아 두게. ——의 제후가 여기 와 계시네.

translation.en: He is much pleased with my company; and having heard of my intention to resign, he has invited me to his country house to spend the spring months with him.
translation.kr: 그분은 내가 곁에 있는 것을 아주 흡족해하시는데, 내가 사직하려 한다는 말을 듣고 봄철을 함께 지내자며 시골 별저로 나를 초대하셨네.

translation.en: I shall be left completely my own master; and as we agree on everything but one point, I shall try my fortune and go with him.
translation.kr: 거기서는 온전히 내 마음대로 지낼 수 있을 걸세. 그리고 우리는 한 가지만 빼고 모든 점에서 뜻이 맞으니, 운을 걸고 따라가 보겠네.

raw: APRIL 19.

translation.en: April 19
translation.kr: 4월 19일

raw: Thanks for both your letters. I delayed my reply, and withheld this letter, till I should obtain an answer from the court. I feared my mother might apply to the minister to defeat my purpose. But my request is granted, my resignation is accepted. I shall not recount with what reluctance it was accorded, nor relate what the minister has written: you would only renew your lamentations. The crown prince has sent me a present of five and twenty ducats; and, indeed, such goodness has affected me to tears. For this reason I shall not require from my mother the money for which I lately applied.

translation.en: Thank you for both your letters.
translation.kr: 두 통의 편지 모두 고맙네.

translation.en: I delayed my reply, and held this letter back, until I should have an answer from the court.
translation.kr: 궁정에서 답이 올 때까지 답장을 미루고 이 편지도 부치지 않고 두었네.

translation.en: I feared my mother might apply to the minister to thwart my purpose.
translation.kr: 어머니가 장관께 청을 넣어 내 뜻을 막으실까 걱정스러웠거든.

translation.en: But my request is granted; my resignation is accepted.
translation.kr: 그러나 청은 받아들여졌고, 사직도 수리되었네.

translation.en: I shall not recount how reluctantly it was granted, nor what the minister has written: you would only start your lamentations again.
translation.kr: 얼마나 마지못해 허락했는지, 장관이 무어라 써 보냈는지는 옮기지 않겠네. 자네가 또 한탄을 시작할 테니.

translation.en: The crown prince has sent me a present of twenty-five ducats, and such goodness has moved me to tears.
translation.kr: 황태자께서 이십오 두카트를 선물로 보내 주셨는데, 그 후의에 나는 눈물이 났네.

translation.en: For that reason I shall not need the money from my mother that I asked for lately.
translation.kr: 그러니 요전에 어머니께 청했던 돈은 필요하지 않게 되었네.

raw: MAY 5.

translation.en: May 5
translation.kr: 5월 5일

raw: I leave this place to-morrow; and, as my native place is only six miles from the high road, I intend to visit it once more, and recall the happy dreams of my childhood. I shall enter at the same gate through which I came with my mother, when, after my father's death, she left that delightful retreat to immure herself in your melancholy town. Adieu, my dear friend: you shall hear of my future career.

translation.en: I leave this place tomorrow; and since my native town is only six miles off the high road, I mean to visit it once more and call back the happy dreams of my childhood.
translation.kr: 내일 이곳을 떠나네. 그리고 내 고향이 큰길에서 육 마일밖에 떨어져 있지 않으니, 한 번 더 들러 어린 시절의 행복한 꿈들을 불러내 볼 생각일세.

translation.en: I shall go in at the same gate I came out of with my mother, when, after my father's death, she left that delightful retreat to shut herself up in your melancholy town.
translation.kr: 아버지가 돌아가신 뒤 어머니가 그 정겨운 곳을 떠나 자네들의 그 우울한 마을에 스스로를 가두러 나오실 때, 나와 함께 나섰던 바로 그 문으로 들어가려 하네.

translation.en: Adieu, my dear friend; you shall hear how I get on.
translation.kr: 잘 있게, 친구여. 내가 어떻게 지내는지 소식 전하겠네.

raw: MAY 9.

translation.en: May 9
translation.kr: 5월 9일

raw: I have paid my visit to my native place with all the devotion of a pilgrim, and have experienced many unexpected emotions. Near the great elm tree, which is a quarter of a league from the village, I got out of the carriage, and sent it on before, that alone, and on foot, I might enjoy vividly and heartily all the pleasure of my recollections. I stood there under that same elm which was formerly the term and object of my walks. How things have since changed! Then, in happy ignorance, I sighed for a world I did not know, where I hoped to find every pleasure and enjoyment which my heart could desire; and now, on my return from that wide world, O my friend, how many disappointed hopes and unsuccessful plans have I brought back!

translation.en: I have paid my visit to my native town with all the devotion of a pilgrim, and have felt many emotions I did not expect.
translation.kr: 순례자의 온 정성으로 고향을 찾았고, 생각지도 못한 감정들을 여럿 느꼈네.

translation.en: Near the great elm, a quarter of a league from the village, I got out of the carriage and sent it on ahead, so that alone and on foot I might enjoy all the pleasure of my recollections vividly and with my whole heart.
translation.kr: 마을에서 오 리쯤 떨어진 큰 느릅나무 곁에서 마차를 내려 먼저 보내고, 홀로 걸으며 추억의 즐거움을 온 마음으로 생생히 누리려 했네.

translation.en: I stood there under the same elm that was once the goal and end of all my walks.
translation.kr: 한때 내 모든 산책의 목표이자 끝이었던 바로 그 느릅나무 아래 서 보았네.

translation.en: How things have changed since!
translation.kr: 그 뒤로 세상이 얼마나 달라졌는지!

translation.en: Then, in happy ignorance, I longed for a world I did not know, where I hoped to find every pleasure and enjoyment my heart could want.
translation.kr: 그때는 행복한 무지 속에서, 알지도 못하는 세상을 그리워했네. 마음이 바라는 온갖 기쁨과 즐거움을 거기서 찾으리라 기대하며 말일세.

translation.en: And now, coming back from that wide world, O my friend, how many disappointed hopes and failed plans I have brought back with me!
translation.kr: 그런데 이제 그 넓은 세상에서 돌아오며, 아 친구여, 얼마나 많은 깨진 희망과 어그러진 계획을 안고 왔는지!

raw: As I contemplated the mountains which lay stretched out before me, I thought how often they had been the object of my dearest desires. Here used I to sit for hours together with my eyes bent upon them, ardently longing to wander in the shade of those woods, to lose myself in those valleys, which form so delightful an object in the distance. With what reluctance did I leave this charming spot; when my hour of recreation was over, and my leave of absence expired! I drew near to the village: all the well-known old summerhouses and gardens were recognised again; I disliked the new ones, and all other alterations which had taken place. I entered the village, and all my former feelings returned. I cannot, my dear friend, enter into details, charming as were my sensations: they would be dull in the narration. I had intended to lodge in the market-place, near our old house. As soon as I entered, I perceived that the schoolroom, where our childhood had been taught by that good old woman, was converted into a shop. I called to mind the sorrow, the heaviness, the tears, and oppression of heart, which I experienced in that confinement. Every step produced some particular impression. A pilgrim in the Holy Land does not meet so many spots pregnant with tender recollections, and his soul is hardly moved with greater devotion. One incident will serve for illustration. I followed the course of a stream to a farm, formerly a delightful walk of mine, and paused at the spot, where, when boys, we used to amuse ourselves making ducks and drakes upon the water. I recollected so well how I used formerly to watch the course of that same stream, following it with inquiring eagerness, forming romantic ideas of the countries it was to pass through; but my imagination was soon exhausted: while the water continued flowing farther and farther on, till my fancy became bewildered by the contemplation of an invisible distance. Exactly such, my dear friend, so happy and so confined, were the thoughts of our good ancestors. Their feelings and their poetry were fresh as childhood. And, when Ulysses talks of the immeasurable sea and boundless earth, his epithets are true, natural, deeply felt, and mysterious. Of what importance is it that I have learned, with every schoolboy, that the world is round? Man needs but little earth for enjoyment, and still less for his final repose.

translation.en: As I looked at the mountains stretched out before me, I thought how often they had been the object of my dearest wishes.
translation.kr: 눈앞에 펼쳐진 산들을 바라보며, 저것들이 얼마나 자주 내 가장 간절한 소원의 대상이었던가 생각했네.

translation.en: Here I used to sit for hours with my eyes fixed on them, longing to wander in the shade of those woods and lose myself in those valleys that look so delightful from a distance.
translation.kr: 여기 앉아 몇 시간이고 그 산들에 눈을 박은 채, 저 숲 그늘을 거닐고 멀리서 그토록 고와 보이는 저 골짜기에 나를 잃어버리기를 갈망했었지.

translation.en: How unwillingly I used to leave this charming spot when my hour of recreation was over and my leave had expired!
translation.kr: 놀 시간이 끝나고 허락받은 틈이 다하면, 이 정겨운 자리를 떠나기가 얼마나 싫었던지!

translation.en: I came near the village and knew all the old summerhouses and gardens again; I disliked the new ones, and every other alteration that had been made.
translation.kr: 마을 가까이 가자 옛 정자와 뜰이 다 눈에 익었네. 새로 생긴 것들과 그 밖에 달라진 것은 하나같이 마음에 들지 않았네.

translation.en: I went into the village, and all my former feelings came back.
translation.kr: 마을에 들어서니 옛 감정이 그대로 돌아왔네.

translation.en: I cannot go into details, my dear friend, charming as my sensations were: they would be dull in the telling.
translation.kr: 친구여, 자세히는 못 쓰겠네. 내게는 그토록 정겨웠어도 옮겨 적으면 시시해질 테니.

translation.en: I had meant to lodge in the market-place, near our old house.
translation.kr: 우리 옛집 가까운 장터에 묵을 작정이었네.

translation.en: As soon as I went in, I saw that the schoolroom where that good old woman taught us as children had been turned into a shop.
translation.kr: 들어서자마자, 그 마음씨 좋은 노파가 우리를 가르치던 교실이 가게로 바뀌어 있는 것을 보았네.

translation.en: I remembered the sorrow, the heaviness, the tears, the oppression of heart I felt in that confinement.
translation.kr: 그 좁은 데 갇혀 느꼈던 서러움과 답답함과 눈물과 짓눌린 가슴이 떠올랐네.

translation.en: Every step brought its own particular impression.
translation.kr: 한 걸음 한 걸음이 저마다 다른 느낌을 불러왔네.

translation.en: A pilgrim in the Holy Land does not meet so many places charged with tender recollections, nor is his soul moved with much greater devotion.
translation.kr: 성지를 찾은 순례자라 해도 그토록 많은 애틋한 기억이 깃든 자리를 만나지는 못할 것이고, 그 영혼이 훨씬 더 깊이 흔들리지도 않을 걸세.

translation.en: One incident will serve as an illustration.
translation.kr: 한 가지 일만 들어 보겠네.

translation.en: I followed the course of a stream down to a farm — once a favourite walk of mine — and stopped at the spot where, as boys, we used to amuse ourselves skimming stones across the water.
translation.kr: 한때 내가 즐겨 걷던 길을 따라 시내를 끼고 농장까지 내려가, 어릴 적 동무들과 물수제비를 뜨며 놀던 자리에 멈춰 섰네.

translation.en: I remembered so clearly how I used to watch the course of that same stream, following it with eager curiosity, forming romantic ideas about the countries it would pass through.
translation.kr: 그 물길을 얼마나 열심히 눈으로 좇으며, 그 물이 흘러갈 나라들을 두고 온갖 낭만적인 상상을 지어내었던지 또렷이 기억나네.

translation.en: But my imagination was soon exhausted, while the water went on flowing further and further, until my fancy was lost in the thought of an invisible distance.
translation.kr: 그러나 내 상상은 이내 바닥나는데 물은 저 멀리 자꾸만 흘러가, 마침내 내 공상은 보이지 않는 먼 곳에 대한 생각 속에 길을 잃곤 했네.

translation.en: Exactly so, my dear friend, so happy and so confined, were the thoughts of our good ancestors.
translation.kr: 친구여, 우리 선한 조상들의 생각이 꼭 그러했네. 그토록 행복하고 그토록 좁았지.

translation.en: Their feelings and their poetry were as fresh as childhood.
translation.kr: 그들의 감정과 시는 어린 시절처럼 싱싱했네.

translation.en: And when Ulysses speaks of the immeasurable sea and the boundless earth, his words are true, natural, deeply felt, and full of mystery.
translation.kr: 그리고 오디세우스가 가없는 바다와 끝없는 땅을 말할 때, 그 말은 참되고 자연스럽고 깊이 느껴지며 신비로 가득하네.

translation.en: What does it matter that I have learned, along with every schoolboy, that the world is round?
translation.kr: 세상이 둥글다는 것을 여느 학동들과 함께 배웠다는 것이 무슨 대수인가?

translation.en: A man needs little earth to enjoy himself on, and less still for his final rest.
translation.kr: 사람이 살아 누리는 데는 땅이 얼마 필요하지 않고, 마지막으로 쉬는 데는 더더욱 적게 든다네.

raw: I am at present with the prince at his hunting lodge. He is a man with whom one can live happily. He is honest and unaffected. There are, however, some strange characters about him, whom I cannot at all understand. They do not seem vicious, and yet they do not carry the appearance of thoroughly honest men. Sometimes I am disposed to believe them honest, and yet I cannot persuade myself to confide in them. It grieves me to hear the prince occasionally talk of things which he has only read or heard of, and always with the same view in which they have been represented by others.

translation.en: I am at present with the prince at his hunting lodge.
translation.kr: 나는 지금 제후와 함께 그분의 사냥 별저에 있네.

translation.en: He is a man one can live happily with.
translation.kr: 함께 지내기 편안한 분일세.

translation.en: He is honest and unaffected.
translation.kr: 정직하고 꾸밈이 없네.

translation.en: There are, however, some strange characters about him whom I cannot make out at all.
translation.kr: 다만 그 둘레에 도무지 속을 알 수 없는 묘한 인물들이 몇 있네.

translation.en: They do not seem vicious, and yet they do not look thoroughly honest either.
translation.kr: 악해 보이지는 않는데, 그렇다고 아주 정직해 보이지도 않네.

translation.en: Sometimes I am inclined to think them honest, and still I cannot bring myself to trust them.
translation.kr: 때로는 정직하다고 여기고 싶어지면서도, 끝내 믿음이 가지는 않네.

translation.en: It grieves me to hear the prince talk now and then of things he has only read or heard about, and always from the point of view in which others have presented them.
translation.kr: 그 제후가 이따금 읽거나 들은 것만으로, 그것도 늘 남이 제시한 관점 그대로 이야기하는 것을 들으면 나는 마음이 아프네.

raw: He values my understanding and talents more highly than my heart, but I am proud of the latter only. It is the sole source of everything of our strength, happiness, and misery. All the knowledge I possess every one else can acquire, but my heart is exclusively my own.

translation.en: He values my understanding and my talents more highly than my heart, and my heart is the only thing I am proud of.
translation.kr: 그분은 내 이해력과 재주를 내 마음보다 높이 치는데, 내가 자랑스러워하는 것은 오직 마음뿐일세.

translation.en: It is the sole source of everything — of our strength, our happiness, and our misery.
translation.kr: 그것이야말로 모든 것의 유일한 샘이니 — 우리 힘도 행복도 불행도 거기서 나오네.

translation.en: All the knowledge I have, anyone else can acquire; but my heart is mine alone.
translation.kr: 내가 지닌 지식이야 누구든 얻을 수 있네. 그러나 내 마음은 오직 내 것일세.

raw: MAY 25.

translation.en: May 25
translation.kr: 5월 25일

raw: I have had a plan in my head of which I did not intend to speak to you until it was accomplished: now that it has failed, I may as well mention it. I wished to enter the army, and had long been desirous of taking the step. This, indeed, was the chief reason for my coming here with the prince, as he is a general in the service. I communicated my design to him during one of our walks together. He disapproved of it, and it would have been actual madness not to have listened to his reasons.

translation.en: I have had a plan in my head which I did not mean to speak of until it was accomplished; now that it has failed, I may as well tell you.
translation.kr: 이루기 전에는 말하지 않으려던 계획이 하나 있었네. 이제 어그러졌으니 털어놓아도 되겠지.

translation.en: I wanted to enter the army, and had wished to take that step for a long time.
translation.kr: 나는 군에 들어가고 싶었고, 오래전부터 그 뜻을 품고 있었네.

translation.en: It was indeed the chief reason for my coming here with the prince, since he is a general in the service.
translation.kr: 제후를 따라 여기 온 가장 큰 까닭도 실은 그것이었네. 그분이 현역 장군이시니 말일세.

translation.en: I told him my design during one of our walks together.
translation.kr: 함께 걷던 어느 날 내 뜻을 말씀드렸네.

translation.en: He disapproved of it, and it would have been sheer madness not to listen to his reasons.
translation.kr: 그분은 반대하셨는데, 그 이유를 듣고도 따르지 않는다면 그야말로 미친 짓이었을 걸세.

raw: JUNE 11.

translation.en: June 11
translation.kr: 6월 11일

raw: Say what you will, I can remain here no longer. Why should I remain? Time hangs heavy upon my hands. The prince is as gracious to me as any one could be, and yet I am not at my ease. There is, indeed, nothing in common between us. He is a man of understanding, but quite of the ordinary kind. His conversation affords me no more amusement than I should derive from the perusal of a well-written book. I shall remain here a week longer, and then start again on my travels. My drawings are the best things I have done since I came here. The prince has a taste for the arts, and would improve if his mind were not fettered by cold rules and mere technical ideas. I often lose patience, when, with a glowing imagination, I am giving expression to art and nature, he interferes with learned suggestions, and uses at random the technical phraseology of artists.

translation.en: Say what you like, I can stay here no longer.
translation.kr: 무어라 하든, 나는 여기 더 머물 수 없네.

translation.en: Why should I stay?
translation.kr: 머물러서 무엇 하겠나?

translation.en: Time hangs heavy on my hands.
translation.kr: 시간이 무겁게 흘러가네.

translation.en: The prince is as gracious to me as anyone could be, and yet I am not at my ease.
translation.kr: 제후는 누구보다 나를 너그럽게 대해 주시는데도 나는 마음이 편치 않네.

translation.en: There is nothing in common between us.
translation.kr: 우리 사이에는 통하는 것이 없네.

translation.en: He is a man of understanding, but quite of the ordinary kind.
translation.kr: 이해력이 있는 분이지만 아주 평범한 종류일세.

translation.en: His conversation gives me no more amusement than I should get from reading a well-written book.
translation.kr: 그분과 나누는 이야기는 잘 쓰인 책 한 권을 읽는 것만큼의 재미도 주지 못하네.

translation.en: I shall stay a week longer, and then set out on my travels again.
translation.kr: 한 주 더 머물다가 다시 길을 나설 참일세.

translation.en: My drawings are the best things I have done since I came here.
translation.kr: 여기 온 뒤로 내가 한 일 가운데 가장 나은 것은 그림일세.

translation.en: The prince has a taste for the arts, and would improve if his mind were not fettered by cold rules and mere technical notions.
translation.kr: 제후는 예술에 취미가 있고, 차가운 규칙과 기교에 관한 관념에 마음이 묶여 있지만 않다면 더 나아지실 분이지.

translation.en: I often lose patience when, with a glowing imagination, I am giving expression to art and nature, and he breaks in with learned suggestions and throws about the technical phrases of artists at random.
translation.kr: 내가 달아오른 상상으로 예술과 자연을 말하고 있을 때 그분이 유식한 참견을 끼워 넣고 화가들의 전문 용어를 아무렇게나 내던지면, 나는 자주 참을성을 잃네.

raw: JULY 16.

translation.en: July 16
translation.kr: 7월 16일

raw: Once more I am a wanderer, a pilgrim, through the world. But what else are you!

translation.en: Once more I am a wanderer, a pilgrim through the world.
translation.kr: 나는 또다시 떠도는 자, 이 세상을 지나는 순례자가 되었네.

translation.en: But what else are you!
translation.kr: 그러나 자네들인들 무엇이 다른가!

raw: JULY 18.

translation.en: July 18
translation.kr: 7월 18일

raw: Whither am I going? I will tell you in confidence. I am obliged to continue a fortnight longer here, and then I think it would be better for me to visit the mines in—. But I am only deluding myself thus. The fact is, I wish to be near Charlotte again, that is all. I smile at the suggestions of my heart, and obey its dictates.

translation.en: Where am I going?
translation.kr: 내가 어디로 가느냐고?

translation.en: I will tell you in confidence.
translation.kr: 자네에게만 털어놓겠네.

translation.en: I am obliged to stay here another fortnight, and then I think it would be better for me to visit the mines in ——.
translation.kr: 여기 두 주를 더 머물러야 하고, 그다음에는 ——의 광산을 둘러보는 편이 낫겠다 싶네.

translation.en: But I am only deceiving myself with that.
translation.kr: 그러나 이것은 나 자신을 속이는 말일 뿐일세.

translation.en: The fact is, I want to be near Charlotte again; that is all.
translation.kr: 실은 다시 샤를로테 가까이 있고 싶은 것이네. 그뿐일세.

translation.en: I smile at what my heart suggests, and I obey it.
translation.kr: 내 마음이 시키는 것에 나는 웃으면서도, 결국 그대로 따르네.

raw: JULY 29.

translation.en: July 29
translation.kr: 7월 29일

raw: No, no! it is yet well all is well! I her husband! O God, who gave me being, if thou hadst destined this happiness for me, my whole life would have been one continual thanksgiving! But I will not murmur—forgive these tears, forgive these fruitless wishes. She—my wife! Oh, the very thought of folding that dearest of Heaven's creatures in my arms! Dear Wilhelm, my whole frame feels convulsed when I see Albert put his arms around her slender waist!

translation.en: No, no! It is well yet — all is well!
translation.kr: 아니야, 아니야! 아직은 괜찮네 — 다 괜찮아!

translation.en: I, her husband!
translation.kr: 내가, 그 사람의 남편이라니!

translation.en: O God, who gave me being, if you had destined this happiness for me, my whole life would have been one long thanksgiving.
translation.kr: 아, 나를 지으신 하느님이여, 이 행복을 제게 정해 두셨더라면 제 한평생이 끝없는 감사가 되었을 것입니다.

translation.en: But I will not complain — forgive these tears, forgive these fruitless wishes.
translation.kr: 그러나 원망하지는 않겠네 — 이 눈물을, 이 헛된 바람을 용서하게.

translation.en: She — my wife!
translation.kr: 그 사람이 — 내 아내라니!

translation.en: Oh, the very thought of folding the dearest of Heaven's creatures in my arms!
translation.kr: 아, 하늘이 지은 것 가운데 가장 사랑스러운 이를 이 팔에 안는다는 생각만으로도!

translation.en: Dear Wilhelm, my whole frame is convulsed when I see Albert put his arm around her slender waist.
translation.kr: 빌헬름, 알베르트가 그 가는 허리에 팔을 두르는 것을 볼 때면 내 온몸이 뒤틀리네.

raw: And shall I avow it? Why should I not, Wilhelm? She would have been happier with me than with him. Albert is not the man to satisfy the wishes of such a heart. He wants a certain sensibility; he wants—in short, their hearts do not beat in unison. How often, my dear friend, I'm reading a passage from some interesting book, when my heart and Charlotte's seemed to meet, and in a hundred other instances when our sentiments were unfolded by the story of some fictitious character, have I felt that we were made for each other! But, dear Wilhelm, he loves her with his whole soul; and what does not such a love deserve?

translation.en: And shall I admit it?
translation.kr: 그리고 이것을 털어놓아도 될까?

translation.en: Why should I not, Wilhelm?
translation.kr: 못 할 것도 없지 않은가, 빌헬름?

translation.en: She would have been happier with me than with him.
translation.kr: 그 사람은 그와 있는 것보다 나와 있는 편이 더 행복했을 걸세.

translation.en: Albert is not the man to satisfy the wishes of such a heart.
translation.kr: 알베르트는 그런 마음의 바람을 채워 줄 만한 사람이 아니네.

translation.en: He lacks a certain sensibility; he lacks — in short, their hearts do not beat together.
translation.kr: 어떤 섬세함이 없네. 그러니까 — 한마디로 두 사람의 마음은 함께 뛰지 않네.

translation.en: How often, my dear friend, reading a passage in some interesting book, have my heart and Charlotte's seemed to meet!
translation.kr: 친구여, 어떤 흥미로운 책의 한 대목을 읽다가 내 마음과 샤를로테의 마음이 마주치는 듯했던 적이 얼마나 많았던가!

translation.en: And in a hundred other moments, when our feelings were drawn out by the story of some imaginary character, I have felt that we were made for one another.
translation.kr: 그리고 어떤 지어낸 인물의 이야기에 우리 감정이 함께 끌려 나오던 백 번의 순간마다, 나는 우리가 서로를 위해 태어났다고 느꼈네.

translation.en: But, dear Wilhelm, he loves her with his whole soul; and what does a love like that not deserve?
translation.kr: 그러나 빌헬름, 그는 온 영혼으로 그 사람을 사랑하네. 그런 사랑이라면 무엇인들 받을 자격이 없겠는가?

raw: I have been interrupted by an insufferable visit. I have dried my tears, and composed my thoughts. Adieu, my best friend!

translation.en: I have been interrupted by an insufferable visit.
translation.kr: 참을 수 없는 방문 때문에 글이 끊겼네.

translation.en: I have dried my tears and composed my thoughts.
translation.kr: 눈물을 닦고 생각을 가라앉혔네.

translation.en: Adieu, my best friend!
translation.kr: 잘 있게, 가장 좋은 벗이여!
